description: Bhṛgu, deprived of breath by Varuṇa, sees in the quarters men cutting up and eating men and other retributions, explained as the fruits of acts in this world without the knowing Agnihotra.
The consecrated sacrificer lives as an embryo: in the hut-womb, wrapped in membranes, with clenched fists, until reborn at the final bath.
The seers 'saw' the hymns when Brahman the self-existent came upon them in austerity; they had direct vision of dharma.
After death one recognizes oneself ('this I am') and one's world; another, bewildered by fire and choked by smoke, does not.
In sleep the breaths go into the self and one knows nothing by mind, speech, smell, sight or hearing.
Disappearing, recollection, radiance, far sight and hearing, entering another body and creating objects at will are the signs of yogic success.
Portents in the world — images of the gods laughing, weeping or sweating, strange births, signs in sky and fire — announce misfortune and are to be appeased by rites.
Naciketas, given to Death, stays three nights unfed in Death's house and receives three boons.
